title: Chimeric music reveals an interaction of pitch and time in electrophysiological signatures of music encoding
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from 27 participants listening to original and chimeric music stimuli designed to investigate pitch-time interactions in music encoding. Chimeric music pairs two distinct melodies with exchanged pitch contours and note onset-times, thereby dissociating pitch and temporal patterns while preserving marginal statistics. The study employs electrophysiological recordings to characterize how the brain encodes musical information when these fundamental acoustic dimensions are decorrelated.
methods_description: EEG data were collected from 27 subjects (age 22.9 ± 3.9 years) with normal hearing and English as primary language. The experiment consisted of two phases: (1) ten one-minute click trials for baseline, and (2) 33 trials each of original and chimeric monophonic music clips presented in shuffled order with 0.5 s inter-trial intervals. Stimuli were presented at 60 dB SPL through ER-2 insert earphones at 48 kHz sampling rate. Participants were seated in a sound-isolating booth approximately 60 cm from a 24-inch monitor. EEG was recorded in BrainVision format. Data collection occurred September-November 2023.
